xccdf-1.2:Benchmark.xccdf-1.2:description: This guide provides security configuration guidance for the Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D BACnet/IP Sedona Unitary Controller 4.

xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:title: Application Development STIG Profile for Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D 4
xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:description: This profile contains BAScontrol22D rules derived from the Application Security and Development STIG requirements that the device appears capable of meeting through its current web interface.

xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:title: Standard Security Profile for Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D4
xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:description: This profile provides a standard security baseline for the Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D BACnet/IP Sedona Unitary Controller 4.

xccdf-1.2:Group.xccdf-1.2:title: Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D4
xccdf-1.2:Group.xccdf-1.2:description: Security configuration guidance for the Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D BACnet/IP Sedona Unitary Controller 4.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Change the Default BAScontrol Admin Password
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: The BAScontrol22D web interface allows the local administrative password to be configured under System Config > Admin. The default password must be changed to a site-approved value before the controller is placed into service.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Built-in or vendor-default credentials are commonly known and can allow unauthorized administrative access if left unchanged.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Maintain BAScontrol22D on a Current Approved Firmware Revision
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D displays its firmware revision on the main interface and in System Status. The controller should be maintained on a current, approved firmware revision.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Firmware updates address product defects and security vulnerabilities and help maintain the controller in a supported and defensible state.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Disable FTP in BAScontrol22D
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D exposes an FTP protocol toggle under System Config > Admin > Enable Protocol. FTP should be disabled unless it is explicitly required and approved for the deployment.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Disabling unused or unapproved protocols reduces attack surface and helps ensure the device uses only functions, ports, and protocols authorized for operation.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Enable NTP Time Synchronization
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D provides Network Time Protocol (NTP) settings under Set Time > NTP Configuration. NTP should be enabled and configured to use an approved time source.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Time synchronization supports consistent event and log timestamps and improves the reliability of operational and security record review.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Use a Static IP Address for Fixed BAScontrol22D Installations
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D provides an IP Mode setting under System Config > Wired/IP. For fixed installations, the controller should use a static IP configuration rather than DHCP.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Static addressing supports predictable network management, simplifies access control policy enforcement, and reduces the risk of unexpected address changes on operational technology networks.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Configure BAScontrol22D Timezone to Map to UTC or GMT
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D provides a timezone selector under Set Time > NTP Configuration. The configured timezone should map to UTC or GMT as required by the deployment.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Timezone configuration that maps cleanly to UTC or GMT supports consistent interpretation of device log timestamps across systems and locations.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Disable Unused BAScontrol22D Protocols
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D exposes protocol toggles under System Config > Admin > Enable Protocol. Only protocols required for the deployment should remain enabled.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Disabling unused protocols reduces attack surface and limits exposure of management and automation interfaces to only those services required for operation.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Maintain a Known-Good BASbackup Configuration
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: BAScontrol22D provides a BASbackup function from the main interface. A known-good backup of the controller configuration should be saved after the device is commissioned and after authorized configuration changes.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Configuration backups support rapid recovery after security incidents, misconfiguration, or device replacement and help restore the controller to a known-good state.

xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:title: Verify the BAScontrol22D4 Controller Identity
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:description: The managed device must be verified as a Contemporary Controls BAScontrol22D BACnet/IP Sedona Unitary Controller 4 before applying this security baseline.
xccdf-1.2:Rule.xccdf-1.2:rationale: Confirming the controller model and hardware revision prevents compliance results and configuration changes from being applied to an unsupported device.

ocil:questionnaire.ocil:title: Change the Default BAScontrol Admin Password
Maintain BAScontrol22D on a Current Approved Firmware Revision
Use a Static IP Address for Fixed BAScontrol22D Installations
Configure BAScontrol22D Timezone to Map to UTC or GMT

ocil:boolean_question.ocil:question_text: Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. Review the configured administrative account and verify the password has been changed from the vendor-default value to an organization-approved password. If the administrative password is still set to the default value, this is a finding. Is it the case that the BAScontrol22D admin password is still set to the default value?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and review the displayed firmware revision. Compare the installed revision to the currently approved firmware baseline for the deployment or the latest vendor-approved revision in local maintenance guidance. If the controller firmware is out of date or not approved for deployment, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller firmware is not current or not approved for deployment?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. In the Enable Protocol section, verify the FTP option is not selected. If FTP is enabled without explicit authorization, this is a finding. Is it the case that FTP is enabled on the controller?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open Set Time. In the NTP Configuration section, verify:
- NTP Enabled is selected - NTP Server is set to an approved time source - Refresh is configured according to site requirements
If NTP is disabled or not configured with an approved time source, this is a finding. Is it the case that NTP is not enabled or is not configured with an approved time server?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Wired/IP. Review the IP Mode setting. For fixed installations, verify it is set to STATIC and that the configured address, netmask, and gateway values match the approved network design. If a fixed installation is configured for DHCP, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller is configured to use DHCP for a fixed installation?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open Set Time. In the NTP Configuration section, review the configured Time Zone value and verify it maps to UTC or GMT as required by the site. If the configured timezone does not map to UTC or GMT, this is a finding. Is it the case that the BAScontrol22D timezone is not configured to map to UTC or GMT?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. In the Enable Protocol section, review the configured protocol set, including BACnet/IP, Sedona, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus, Wall Setter, and FTP when present. Verify that only the protocols required for the approved deployment remain enabled. If unnecessary protocols remain enabled, this is a finding. Is it the case that one or more unused BAScontrol22D protocols remain enabled?

Access the BAScontrol22D main interface and verify that the BASbackup function has been used to save a current known-good configuration. Review local administrative records or the designated backup repository and confirm that a recent backup exists for the deployed controller. If a current BASbackup configuration is not available, this is a finding. Is it the case that a current BASbackup configuration is not available?

Using the controller's approved management interface, review its device information and verify that the model is BAScontrol22D and the hardware revision is 4. If the model or hardware revision does not match, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller cannot be identified as a supported BAScontrol22D4 device?
